articles.body: How to Make Your Social Media Text Stand Out Without Installing Fonts Have you ever wanted to make your social media bio or posts look different without installing extra fonts or apps? One simple option is to use Unicode text characters . What Is Unicode Text? Unicode is a standard that helps computers represent text across different languages and writing systems. It also includes mathematical alphanumeric characters that can look bold, italic, or decorative. For example: Regular: Hello World Bold: 𝐇𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐨 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 Bold italic: 𝑯𝒆𝒍𝒍𝒐 𝑾𝒐𝒓𝒍𝒅 These styles use different Unicode characters rather than simply applying a bold font setting to regular letters. Where Can You Use Stylish Text?

articles.title: 1,000+ Mathematicians vow to Shun AI in Scientific Research
articles.excerpt: 1,000+ Mathematicians vow to Shun AI in Scientific Research On October 22, 2026, at 01:57 UTC, a group of over a thousand mathematicians globallyization pledged to exclude artificial intelligence from…
articles.body: 1,000+ Mathematicians vow to Shun AI in Scientific Research On October 22, 2026, at 01:57 UTC, a group of over a thousand mathematicians globallyization pledged to exclude artificial intelligence from their research processes. This isn't just a technical preference; it is a fundamental defense of human logic and rigorous intellectual verification. The signatories argue that while AI can process vast datasets and suggest potential patterns, it lacks the deep conceptual reasoning and creative intuition required for true mathematical breakthroughs. By rejecting AI-generated proofs, these researchers are prioritizing the integrity of the scientific method over the speed offered by automated tools.

Here's what we learned, step by step. 1. Answers from your own history (no automation yet) The agent searches wiki pages and issues with Redmine's native search, as the user who asked . International Sloth Day was October 20, and sloths have the right idea. They move at their own pace, conserve their energy, and let the world come to them. So for this week's challenge I built the most sloth-shaped thing I could think of: a tool for people who want music to wind down to but cannot be bothered to browse, curate, or pay for another subscription. You type a lazy vibe — "rainy sunday piano", "slow ambient for sleep", "fireplace while it snows" — and Sloth Sounds writes the music. One command gets you a seamless loop.

articles.title: Steer, Don’t Rewrite: Annotate Agent Trajectories 2 Faster in Live Environments with onPanda
articles.excerpt: Dynamically connect to agent environments and annotate multi-turn SFT and preference data with tool_calls and reasoning online Existing agent annotation tools (such as Potato and Argilla) mostly suppo…
articles.body: Dynamically connect to agent environments and annotate multi-turn SFT and preference data with tool_calls and reasoning online Existing agent annotation tools (such as Potato and Argilla ) mostly support assigning attributes or adding textual feedback to completed trajectories. However, editing trajectories to construct high-quality multi-turn agent SFT data presents two core challenges: Coupled environment state : Agent trajectories alternate between tool calls ( tool_calls ) and environment feedback ( tool messages). Once a tool call in a given turn is modified, the original subsequent trajectory is usually no longer valid—the corrected call must be executed in the real environment, and generation must continue from the new feedback.

articles.excerpt: Google sent us a legal notice this month. We're not in trouble: every Google Workspace and Cloud admin got the notice. It covers Google's new AI agent terms, effective 12 Oct 2026, which update the Go…
articles.body: Google sent us a legal notice this month. We're not in trouble: every Google Workspace and Cloud admin got the notice. It covers Google's new AI agent terms, effective 12 Oct 2026, which update the Google Workspace Service Specific Terms and the Google Cloud Terms of Service. The headline is in the Workspace terms: the customer is "solely responsible" for any Agentic AI Action. This is the developer version: what the terms say, then what to actually change. The three clauses that matter Cloud terms 3.3 now restricts using "the Services or any AI Agent ... in violation of the AUP" (the Acceptable Use Policy). Cloud terms 13.2: you indemnify Google for "Customer's or an End User's use of the Services or AI Agents in breach of the AUP or Section 3.3 (Restrictions)".

articles.title: Faster to Science: A Letter to the Science Community
articles.excerpt: NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall.
articles.body: Dear NASA Science Community, NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall, from NASA Headquarters, to explain our new Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), and answer your questions. We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long. It has taken years to move mission concepts through the current two-step process. This has often come with contract management challenges, unpredictability, and not enough funding. NASA is committed to doing better — and I’m excited to share with you how we’re making it happen.

articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.
